I included the share-price moves because I read the evidence rule as covering statements of figures about the company, and I treated stock-price figures as company figures. The rule I applied was: "A material statement is one of four kinds. (1) The company's own figure, guidance or decision..." and "Go through the item from its first paragraph to its last and take every statement of these kinds."

The instruction you're pointing to says to reject "an investor's position or a share-price move ('he is short the stock'; 'shares fell 13% this month')." I set that rejection rule aside. I should not have. The rejection explicitly names share-price moves as out of scope, and it is more specific than the general rule that every figure counts, so it should have controlled. The specific exclusion overrides the general inclusion.

I also set aside, in part, the instruction on author views. The item is opinion (T8), and the output instructions say to read out the author's forecasts, ratings and price targets and the facts the author cites with their attribution. Several of my entries are the author's historical stock-performance claims, which are cited facts rather than the author's own arguments, so they are not clearly excluded. But the share-price framing still matches the explicit reject example, and I should have weighed that.

Looking at the item as a whole, the statements that fall outside the share-price exclusion include the $4.7 trillion market capitalisation, which is a market-value figure rather than a price move, and the description of earnings-report reactions (e6). Those are borderline under the same rule and should be judged against it, not assumed in.
